arguments.summary: Company contribution: the supplied evidence supports conditional EPS/multiple stress tests, not a fair-value ranking. NVDA’s bridge rests on Q3 FY27 guidance and an assumed Q4 continuation; MU’s bridge directly incorporates its Q4 FY26 guidance but FY26 had ended and remained unreported as of the cutoff. QQQ provides diversified—not zero—issuer-specific exposure through dated NVDA and MU holdings.

claims.text: NVDA reported FY27 H1 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.85; Q2 revenue was $96.221bn and GAAP diluted EPS $2.46. Its Q3 FY27 outlook was $108.0bn revenue ±2%, 74.0% GAAP gross margin ±50bp and about $9.2bn GAAP opex, explicitly assuming no China Data Center compute revenue.

NVDA FY27 GAAP sensitivity uses assumed EPS/P-E pairs of $9.50/19x, $10.10/22x and $10.70/25x. The residual after reported H1 EPS is respectively $4.65, $5.25 and $5.85 under a constant diluted-share approximation—not an exact annual EPS reconciliation. Thus bear tests low-end Q3 execution plus Q4 demand/mix normalization; base requires Q3 guidance achievement and broadly sustained Q4 earnings; bull requires high-end execution and continued AI-infrastructure demand/margin resilience.

At NVDA’s split-adjusted September 18 close, the conditional bear/base/bull changes are -18.7925%, -0.0315% and +20.3491%. Bull upside exceeds bear-loss magnitude by 1.5567 percentage points, a near-balanced, unweighted stress asymmetry rather than a probability-weighted skew. In the base case, the close equates to 22.0069x on assumed $10.10 EPS, or $10.1032 EPS at held-fixed 22x; exceeding the close requires exceeding one of those thresholds while holding the other input fixed. A Q3 shortfall, Q4 demand/mix normalization, or lower multiple would reverse the base condition.

MU reported FY26 first-nine-month GAAP diluted EPS of $41.40. FQ3 revenue was $41.456bn and GAAP diluted EPS $24.67; its FQ4 guidance was $50.0bn revenue ±$1.0bn, approximately 86% GAAP gross margin and GAAP diluted EPS of $30.73 ±$1.00. High-volume HBM4 shipments and product ramps are stated demand-supporting operating developments, but are not proof that guidance will be met.

MU FY26 sensitivity uses assumed EPS/P-E pairs of $69.00/12x, $72.13/14x and $74.00/16x. Residual EPS is $27.60, $30.73 and $32.60 under a constant diluted-share approximation; the base residual mechanically equals guided FQ4 GAAP EPS midpoint, while bear and bull test low/high guide outcomes with execution/mix pressure or continued AI-memory demand and margin execution. FY26 ended August 27 and its actual FQ4 result was not in supplied evidence, so this is a provisional historical bridge, not next-year growth.

At MU’s split-adjusted September 18 close, conditional bear/base/bull changes are -18.4879%, -0.5887% and +16.5584%. Bear downside exceeds bull upside by 1.9295 percentage points. The base close-equating thresholds are 14.0829x on assumed $72.13 EPS or $72.5571 EPS at held-fixed 14x; merely reaching either threshold equates value to the dated close, while exceeding it requires higher EPS or multiple with the other held fixed. FQ4 below guidance, memory-demand/margin deterioration, or multiple compression reverses the base condition.

QQQ’s sponsor-reported aggregate P/E was 30.08 as of August 31, with 103 holdings reported as of September 10. Its dated September 18 holdings showed NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336%; these are dated fund composition data, not current holdings or an investor’s portfolio exposure.

Compared with direct NVDA or MU exposure, QQQ diversifies issuer-specific earnings and multiple shocks across its reported holdings but retains meaningful dated exposure to both companies. QQQ’s sponsor aggregate P/E is not methodologically interchangeable with the companies’ deliberately hypothetical annual GAAP EPS/P-E stress inputs; therefore neither the 30.08 aggregate P/E nor the 19x–25x and 12x–16x scenario bands establishes a fair or preferable valuation.

gaps.description: No actual MU FQ4/FY26 result or quarterly diluted-share count is supplied. FY26 ended August 27, so the FY26 EPS grid remains a qualified, constant-share provisional bridge rather than reported annual earnings.

No empirical company multiple history, consensus, or matched earnings-date/market-multiple methodology is supplied. Scenario multiples are useful unweighted stresses but cannot support an unconditional fair-value or cross-symbol valuation ranking.

QQQ holdings are dated September 18 and the sponsor aggregate P/E is dated August 31; weights/metrics can change, and the corporate sensitivity grids cannot quantify QQQ’s aggregate earnings sensitivity.

assumptions: All scenario-grid EPS and P/E inputs are explicit unweighted assumptions, not consensus, observed multiples, forecasts, probabilities, or price targets.
NVDA grid is FY27 GAAP diluted EPS for January 26, 2026–January 25, 2027; MU grid is FY26 GAAP diluted EPS for August 29, 2025–August 27, 2026. Both differ from the 63-session research horizon.
Residual EPS calculations use a constant diluted-share approximation despite reported quarterly share-count variation; scenario-grid prices use split-adjusted closes.
arguments.counter_thesis: Demand durability may be overstated: NVDA’s Q4 could normalize after Q3 even if guidance is met, and MU’s FQ4 could miss its guide or margins could weaken. Conversely, higher demand/margins can coexist with valuation compression. QQQ reduces single-issuer dependence but does not eliminate it because both issuers are dated holdings.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA when Q3 results/outlook disclose whether revenue, gross margin, and Data Center demand meet or miss the supplied Q3 guidance; a miss or weaker Q4 outlook invalidates the base residual-EPS bridge, while stronger Q4 continuation supports reassessing it.

Review MU upon FQ4/FY26 results: compare actual GAAP EPS, revenue, gross margin and diluted shares with the $30.73 ±$1.00 guided EPS bridge. An outcome below the guide or weaker subsequent outlook shifts the bridge toward/below bear; a high-end result with durable demand supports reassessment.
Review QQQ after the next sponsor holdings and fund-characteristics update; material changes in NVDA/MU weights or aggregate P/E alter the stated overlap and invalidate use of the dated look-through.

shared_exposures.mechanism: AI/data-center demand is a common operating channel: NVDA’s Data Center results/guidance and MU’s HBM4/data-center memory developments support it, while QQQ includes dated weights in both issuers. QQQ aggregation limits direct issuer sensitivity but does not remove the channel.
shared_exposures.qualification: Dated issuer statements and fund composition; no quantified common-demand elasticity or current QQQ holdings inference.
